assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: @TableTest("""...""")

assertions.text: Email validation and name-required error scenarios are present — at least one row for invalid email and one for missing name.
assertions.evidence: Rows: 'Name is null', 'Email is null', 'Email missing @ symbol', 'Email with no domain part'

assertions.text: Dietary requirements and/or accessibility needs use blank cells (null) when not provided — not 'N/A' or 'none'.
assertions.evidence: Columns show blank cells: 'Valid, no optional fields' has empty entries for Dietary Reqs and Accessibility

assertions.text: When testing pricing rules, irrelevant inputs (e.g. dietary requirements don't affect price) use value sets or representative values — not blanks.
assertions.evidence: Pricing table passes null: 'service.register("John Smith", "john@example.com", null, null, registrationDate, groupSize)'

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column in both tables: 'Scenario'

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Result?', 'Price?')
assertions.evidence: 'Accepted?', 'Error Message?', 'Final Price?'

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language — not code identifiers.
assertions.evidence: 'Name', 'Email', 'Dietary Reqs', 'Registration Date', 'Group Size', 'Final Price?'

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions — not outcomes.
assertions.evidence: 'Valid, no optional fields', 'Early-bird, day before cutoff', 'Group of 5, discount applies'

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: Validation method: 'assertEquals(accepted, result.isAccepted());' with no conditionals

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest
assertions.evidence: shouldValidateRegistration: '@DisplayName', '@Description("""...""")', '@TableTest'

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a clear, descriptive method name.
assertions.evidence: @DisplayName("Registration validation") and @DisplayName("Registration pricing")

assertions.text: If @Description is present and longer than a single line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string), not string concatenation.
assertions.evidence: @Description("""...""")

assertions.text: Multiple tables are used, each addressing a distinct concern — validation vs pricing.
assertions.evidence: Two separate methods: 'shouldValidateRegistration' and 'shouldApplyPricing'

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations.
assertions.evidence: Validation has 8 rows; pricing has 6 rows — focused on boundary cases, not Cartesian product

assertions.text: Input validation and pricing/discount calculation are in separate @TableTest methods
assertions.evidence: shouldValidateRegistration and shouldApplyPricing are separate methods

assertions.text: Validation @TableTest includes Dietary Requirements and Accessibility Needs columns, with rows showing both null and non-null values are accepted — not hardcoded as null.
assertions.evidence: Validation table has columns 'Dietary Reqs' and 'Accessibility', with rows 'With dietary requirements' and 'With accessibility needs' showing non-null accepted

assertions.text: Registration date uses descriptive values with @TypeConverter, not raw date literals.
assertions.evidence: Pricing table uses literal dates '2025-05-01', '2025-02-28', '2025-03-01' instead of descriptive labels like 'before cutoff'

assertions.text: If registration dates are literal, the early-bird cutoff date appears as a separate policy column.
assertions.evidence: Literal dates used but no separate cutoff-date column; cutoff only mentioned in @Description text

assertions.text: @Description does not include information already visible in table columns or derived from table structure.
assertions.evidence: @Description states 'Base price is £100... Early-bird (before 2025-03-01): 20% off → £80' which restates discount rules demonstrated in rows

assertions.text: Output column is 'Discount?' (percentage or amount off) rather than 'Price?' — or if 'Price?' is used, both 'Base price' and 'Price?' columns are present.
assertions.evidence: Column is 'Final Price?' but no 'Base price' column present to trace calculation

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method has a single, uniform assertion pattern applied to all rows.
assertions.evidence: Validation: 'assertEquals(accepted, result.isAccepted()); assertEquals(errorMessage, result.getErrorMessage());' uniform across all rows

assertions.text: The optional-fields acceptance table includes an expectation/output column asserting that each combination is accepted.
assertions.evidence: Validation table has 'Accepted?' output column with true values for rows with optional fields

assertions.text: Scenario descriptions do not include specific field values already visible in the table.
assertions.evidence: @Description for pricing states 'Name ("John Smith") and email ("john@example.com") are fixed valid values' — these field identities are already obvious from the test body
